messages:
mia: Quick follow-up to the FP8/INT4 RFC — hit a nasty OOD failure where answers collapse after ~40 tokens when we run the mixed profile (FP8 for attn, 4-bit for MLP). Repro + logs below.

mia: Repro (super small):
```yaml
precision_profile:
  attention: fp8
  mlp: int4
  fallback: [fp16, int8]
batch: 8
seq_len: 512
model: redwood/tiny-test-v2
```
Log snippet: `token_40: <repetition_loop_detected>`, perplexity jump x2.1 at step 40.

devin: ugh. Can you attach the prompt and exact weights? Is this only on that tiny-test model? :thinking:

mia: Prompt is a long instruction + code block (posted privately). Seen on two different checkpoints (v2 and v2a) but only when MLP is in int4 mode + attn fp8. If I force attn->int8 it looks better but cost up.

srini: Sounds like a precision boundary problem where kv cache / attn fp8 interacts poorly with quantized matmuls in MLP. We should treat attention precision as a separate contract: some attention kernels must be >= FP8, otherwise catastrophic drift.

eva: Agree. Operationally we need two things: 1) runtime negotiation semantics (how requester and runtime pick per-subgraph precision) and 2) a rollout gating policy + metrics to catch these regressions early.

luke: For negotiations, propose precedence list and hard-level fallbacks: `preference: [attn:fp8, mlp:int4]` plus `hard_fallback: {attn: fp16}`. If runtime cannot satisfy attn fp8, it must pick fp16 for attn rather than degrade mlp only. That keeps semantics deterministic.

mia: That would have prevented the case — runtime selected int8-attn when fp8 kernels missing and left mlp in int4. We should codify that selection priority.

devin: Implementation sketch: add a small contract blob shipped with model artifacts: `precision_manifest.json`:
```json
{
  "layers": {
    "self_attn": {"min_precision": "fp8", "prefer": "fp8"},
    "mlp": {"min_precision": "int4", "prefer": "int4"}
  },
  "global_fallback": ["fp16", "int8"]
}
```
Runtime evaluates capability matrix vs manifest and picks the highest-priority feasible config. If infeasible, reject or escalate to canary only.

srini: Important: add a `quality_escrow` signal in negotiation — runtime must reserve an escrow to compare key metrics (perplexity_delta, bleu_delta, repetition_rate) for canary traffic before completing the swap. If escrow fails, auto-revert.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary job created for model redwood/tiny-test-v2 with profile "attn:fp8|mlp:int4" — 0.2% traffic. Job id: canary-2245127890-01

eva: Proposed gating thresholds (initial):
- perplexity_delta > 1.2 (vs baseline) -> fail
- repetition_rate increase > 5pct -> fail
- rougeL / bleu drop > 2.5 absolute points -> fail
- p95_latency increase > 30% -> warn (not fail)
Telemetry window: 1k requests or 30 minutes, whichever first.

luke: We should also track layer-wise signals: attn_token_loss_delta specifically for the first 128 tokens to catch early attention collapse.

devin: Storage/ingest cost note: escrow telemetry at per-token resolution is expensive. We can do sampled per-request snapshots with aggregate counters and a small set of golden prompts. Golden prompt evals are cheap and deterministic — run them as part of canary pipeline.

mia: I ran a quick golden set (20 prompts) — int4-mlp + fp8-attn fail rate 8/20 -> big red. int8-attn + int4-mlp had 1/20 fails. So suggests attn fp8 matters but the combination is sensitive.

srini: Actionable plan:
- manifest + runtime selection logic (devin)
- canary pipeline: golden set + escrow metrics + auto-revert (eva)
- add `precision_hint` flag to API/serving config so workloads can prefer picture: `precision_hint: "attn:prefer_fp8"` (mia will draft)
- telemetry sampling policy + cost estimate (devin + ops)

devin: Quick CLI to run local golden set (for reproducibility):
```bash
./tools/run_golden_eval.sh --model redwood/tiny-test-v2 --profile attn=fp8,mlp=int4 --out results.json
jq . summary.json
```

mia: I'll draft a small RFC follow-up with the manifest schema + example, include the golden prompts and error signatures. Will ping for reviews.

eva: One more: include a staged rollout knob: `quality_guardrails: {stage0: 0.2%, stage1: 2%, stage2: 10%, stage3: 100%}` with automated pause on fail. That keeps customer impact minimal.

luke: +1. Also put library-level regression detector that emits `regression_count` and `regression_severity` into tracing for fast search.

mia: Thanks all — I'll open the PR and attach the initial manifest schema and the 20 golden prompts.

devin: If you want, I can wire the runtime check in staging this afternoon.

mia: That would be awesome. I'll drop the private prompt file in the thread. :thumbsup:
